Normalized EPS was $0.42, well above prior guidance of $0.16-$0.19, though this included a one-time ~$100 million IEEPA tariff recovery receivable; excluding this, EPS still beat guidance. Management raised the full-year outlook across all key metrics, citing stronger innovation, distribution gains, and improved execution, while noting input cost inflation headwinds and a cautious view on second-half category trends.

Organic detection sales were flat due to a low single-digit decline in fixed monitoring tied to the Middle East, while industrial PPE grew 16% organically; fire service declined 2% on slower AFG grant orders, but management cited accelerating order momentum and a book-to-bill of approximately 1x, above seasonal trends.

Management continues to push for margins and highlighted growth in Advanced Materials (8%) and Polyurethanes (4%) above underlying markets.
